statement: Find the range of real values of $k$ for which the equation $(k+1)x^{2}-2x+k=0$ has real roots.
solution: For real roots the discriminant must be non-negative: $(-2)^{2}-4(k+1)k\ge 0$, i.e. $4-4k(k+1)\ge 0$, so $k^{2}+k-1\le 0$. The roots of $k^{2}+k-1=0$ are $\tfrac{-1\pm\sqrt5}{2}$, hence $-\tfrac{1+\sqrt5}{2}\le k\le \tfrac{-1+\sqrt5}{2}$.
hints: Solve the resulting quadratic inequality in $k$.
